title: SLO activation field notes and roll-forward plan
content:
Status: draft
Owner: Aisha Patel (platform-engineering lead)
Summary:
A short, pragmatic field guide for staging, measuring, and rolling forward Service Level Objectives across product teams. This doc records lessons from the initial pilot (Search & Chat) and defines a 6-week roll-forward plan to embed SLOs into two additional feature teams (Embeddings and Dedicated). Focus is on low-friction telemetry, gating criteria for production SLO enforcement, and operational handoffs.

Goals (what success looks like)
- Two feature teams adopt and continuously measure at least one availability or latency SLO (baseline + alerting) by end of week 6.
- No more than 1 missed SLO incident in pilot during the roll-forward window (operational maturity target).
- Automated dashboards and synthetic probes running for new services with runbook links.

Scope and exclusions
- In scope: setting SLO targets, implementing synthetic checks, wiring alerts to on-call rotations, runbook creation, staging experiments.
- Out of scope: rewriting model-serving code paths or deep lower-level runtime optimizations (these are handled as downstream tickets).

Quick notes from pilot (observations)
- Synthetic probes reduced false positives once we agreed on 95th/99th percentile windows; initial alerts were too sensitive. Miguel/Terraform script corrections applied.
- Prefix caching increases variance in tail latency; teams must surface median vs p99 on dashboards.
- Alert routing: route degradations to feature on-call first, with SRE backup after 10m.
- Common blocker: missing latency tags in request spans (requires small instrumentation PRs).

Primary stakeholders and roles
- Program lead: Aisha Patel (platform-engineering) — program coordination, weekly sync owner
- SRE partner: Lina Chen — alerting/runbooks/incident playbook
- Product owners: Priya Kapoor (Embeddings), Samir O'Neill (Dedicated) — acceptance and rollout decisions
- Observability eng: Miguel Torres — dashboards, synthetic probe templates, CI checks
- Security & Compliance: optional reviewer for private-deployments pipeline changes

Roll-forward timeline (6 weeks)
Week 0 (this week): kickoff + discovery
- Kickoff meeting (30m) with feature teams, SRE, obs eng. Share pilot learnings and template artifacts.
- Deliverables: SLO template (latency/availability), synthetic probe recipe, runbook scaffold.

Week 1: measurement baseline & instrumentation work
- Feature teams open instrumentation tickets (add latency spans, required tags).
- Observability eng provides probe CI PR template.
- Deliverables: baseline dashboard, open PRs tracked in REL-482.

Week 2: synthetic probes + CI gating
- Deploy probe in staging and run daily for 3 days. Tweak thresholds.
- Create alert policies with 2-step escalation (feature on-call -> SRE).
- Deliverables: probes in staging, alert policies, PRs merged.

Week 3: canary enforcement and runbook draft
- Enable SLO monitoring in canary for limited traffic. Runbooks drafted by SRE partner.
- Mini tabletop drill with feature team and SRE.
- Deliverables: runbook v0.1, drill notes.

Week 4: production activation (soft)
- Turn on SLO alerting in production with long alert windows (graceful). Observe for 72 hours.
- Track noise and tune.
- Deliverables: production alerts active, noise metrics.

Week 5: post-activation retro + adjustments
- Review incidents/alerts, refine thresholds, finalize runbook.
- Deliverables: retro notes, refined thresholds.

Week 6: formal adoption and handoff
- Formal sign-off from product and SRE. Move ownership to feature team with SRE as guardian.
- Deliverables: sign-off doc, handoff checklist completed.

Milestones and gating criteria
- Gating for production alerting: (1) synthetic probes stable for 72h in staging; (2) runbook exists and SRE has participated in a drill; (3) feature on-call roster confirmed.
- Acceptance criteria for adoption: dashboards show consistent baseline for 7 days, <3 alerts per week from noise, runbook actionable within 15 minutes.

Telemetry and measurement plan
- Dashboards: median, p95, p99 latency trends; availability SLI (successful requests / total); probe success rate; incident count.
- Synthetic probes: 1-minute cadence for critical routes, 5-minute cadence for lower priority.
- Alert thresholds: start conservative (p99 > target for 20m) then tighten after 2 weeks.

Runbooks and incident playbooks (outline)
- Triage steps (quick checks), probable causes, mitigation steps (fallback to model variant, capacity scaling), escalation path, postmortem owner.
- Templates located at confluence:REL-SLO-activation-overview (linked).

Budget and staffing notes
- Expected incremental on-call load: +2 pages/month per feature team during first month (estimate).
- Observability engineer time: 0.4 FTE for 6 weeks to create templates and CI checks.

Risks and open questions
- Risk: probe flapping creates alert fatigue. Mitigation: circuit-breaker window and adjustable probe cadence.
- Risk: teams unable to ship small instrumentation changes in time. Mitigation: SRE pair-programming sessions.
- Open question: Do we enforce SLOs at product billing tier or service level? Product owners to decide by Week 2.

Communication plan
- Weekly 30m sync (Wednesdays) — agenda: blockers, metrics, action items.
- Slack channel: #reliability-ops for async updates; use thread per service activation.
- Bi-weekly progress note to platform-eng leadership.

Immediate next actions (this doc owner)
- Schedule kickoff meeting and add agenda to REL-482. (Aisha)
- Observability PR template: Miguel to open by EOD Friday.
- Product decision: Priya and Samir to confirm SLO target ranges by Week 1.

Appendix: templates and quick commands
- Synthetic probe recipe (curl example):
  curl -i -X GET "https://staging.redwood/api/v1/embeddings/probe?seed=1" -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROBE_TOKEN"
- Example alert rule: p99(latency) > 250ms for 20m -> page feature on-call then SRE after 10m
- Quick checklist for runbook completeness: title, owner, triage steps, rollback flag, postmortem owner, links to dashboards.

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep thresholds conservative at first — pilot showed teams prefer fewer noisy pages.
- Coordinate with infra-autoscaler folks for Dedicated capacity spike tests.
- Add a short post-adoption survey for feature teams to collect friction signals.

References
- REL-482 (Jira) — rollout epic
- GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/213 (probe templates)
- Confluence: REL-SLO-activation-overview

-- end of draft --
